examples.ko: 이 지원금은 미혼자도 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Unmarried people can apply for this subsidy too.
Both unmarried and married people took part in the survey.
The proportion of unmarried people is growing every year.

examples.ko: 이 기숙사는 미혼자만 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only unmarried people can move into this dormitory.

examples.ko: 미혼자라고 해서 결혼 생각이 없는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Just because someone is unmarried doesn't mean they have no thoughts of marrying.

examples.ko: 신청서에 미혼자는 이 칸을 비워 두세요.
examples.en: If you are unmarried, leave this box blank on the form.

explain: 서류, 통계, 뉴스에서 '기혼자'와 짝으로 자주 나와요. 평소 대화에서는 '미혼'이나 '결혼 안 한 사람'이라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. 사람을 직접 부를 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It appears in forms, statistics and news as the pair of '기혼자' (married person). In everyday talk people often say '미혼' or '결혼 안 한 사람'. You would not use it to address someone directly.

examples.ko: 제 피부는 민감성이라 화장품을 고를 때 조심해요.
examples.en: I have sensitive skin, so I'm careful when choosing cosmetics.

examples.ko: 민감성 피부에 맞는 크림을 추천해 주세요.
examples.en: Please recommend a cream that suits sensitive skin.

examples.ko: 아이가 먼지에 대한 민감성이 높아서 자주 재채기를 해요.
examples.en: My child is highly sensitive to dust, so he sneezes often.

examples.ko: 의사가 소리에 대한 민감성을 검사해 봤어요.
examples.en: The doctor tested my sensitivity to sound.

examples.ko: 민감성 치약으로 바꿨더니 이가 덜 시려요.
examples.en: After I switched to toothpaste for sensitive teeth, my teeth hurt less from the cold.
Skin sensitivity gets worse during the change of seasons.

explain: '민감성 피부'처럼 화장품, 피부, 치약 이야기에서 가장 많이 만나요. 성격을 말할 때는 '민감하다', 상태를 설명할 때는 '민감성'을 써요. 반대로 둔한 정도는 '둔감하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: You meet it most in phrases like '민감성 피부' (sensitive skin) in talk about cosmetics, skin and toothpaste. Use the adjective '민감하다' to describe a person, and '민감성' to name the condition or trait. The opposite adjective is '둔감하다'.

examples.ko: 이 수족관에서는 민물고기와 바다 어류를 한곳에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: At this aquarium you can see freshwater fish and sea fish in one place.
I made spicy fish stew with freshwater fish caught in the river.
Freshwater fish can't live long in seawater.
My father went out at dawn to catch freshwater fish.
Many freshwater fish live in this river.
That restaurant cooks freshwater fish dishes well.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '바닷물고기'예요. 강이나 호수에 사는 물고기를 말하고, 음식 이야기에서는 매운탕 재료로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '바닷물고기' (saltwater fish). It means fish living in rivers and lakes, and in food talk it often comes up as an ingredient for 매운탕 (spicy fish stew).

examples.en: I go freshwater fishing with my father every weekend.
Freshwater fishing is quieter than sea fishing, so I like it.
Worms are a common bait for freshwater fishing.
Have you tried freshwater fishing too?
I bought new freshwater fishing gear.
A friend suggested going freshwater fishing, so I tagged along.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '바다낚시'예요. 보통 '민물낚시를 가다/하다'라고 말하고, 저수지, 강, 호수에서 하는 낚시를 가리켜요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '바다낚시' (sea fishing). People usually say '민물낚시를 가다/하다', and it refers to fishing in reservoirs, rivers and lakes.

examples.en: It was hot, so I wore a sleeveless T-shirt.

examples.ko: 민소매 원피스는 회사에서 입기 조금 부담돼요.
examples.en: A sleeveless dress feels a bit awkward to wear to the office.
I put a thin cardigan over my sleeveless top.

examples.ko: 이 민소매는 여름에 입기 정말 시원해요.
examples.en: This sleeveless top is really cool to wear in summer.
My arms feel cool in a sleeveless top.

examples.ko: 동생이 민소매 차림으로 나가서 감기에 걸렸어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling went out in a sleeveless outfit and caught a cold.

explain: '민-'은 장식이나 덮는 것이 없다는 느낌을 더해요. 그래서 민소매는 소매가 없는 옷이고, 민얼굴, 민무늬도 같은 방식이에요. 영어의 '나시'는 일본식 표현이라 요즘은 '민소매'라고 하는 게 더 바른 말이에요.
explain_en: The prefix '민-' adds the sense of having nothing extra on it. So 민소매 is a garment with no sleeves, and 민얼굴 and 민무늬 work the same way. People also say '나시', a Japanese-origin word, but '민소매' is the standard Korean term.

examples.en: At the folk village I tried traditional games with the kids.

examples.ko: 민속촌에서는 옛 풍속을 직접 체험해 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: At the folk village you can experience old customs firsthand.
Many foreign tourists visit the folk village.
Do you want to go to the folk village this weekend?
The folk village is a nice place to look around in hanbok.
I also ate traditional food inside the folk village.

explain: 옛날 집과 생활 모습을 보여 주는 관광지를 가리켜요. 특정 장소 이름으로 '한국민속촌'을 줄여 말할 때도 있지만, 일반 명사로도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a tourist site that shows old houses and the way people used to live. People also use it as a short name for 한국민속촌 (the Korean Folk Village), but it works as a common noun too.

examples.en: I came out with a bare face today.
I was told I look prettier without makeup.
I don't want to show my bare face in front of my friends.
That actor's bare face looks very clear too.
I went out wearing only sunscreen on my bare face.
I posted a no-makeup photo and the response was good.

explain: 화장을 하지 않은 얼굴을 말할 때 써요. 비슷한 말로 '맨얼굴'도 많이 쓰는데, 둘 다 같은 뜻으로 말해도 괜찮아요. 보통 '민얼굴로 나가다', '민얼굴을 보이다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for a face with no makeup on. '맨얼굴' is a common alternative, and you can use either to mean the same thing. It usually appears in patterns like '민얼굴로 나가다' and '민얼굴을 보이다'.

examples.ko: 시행 첫날부터 시청 민원실에 문의 전화가 몰렸어요.
examples.en: From the first day it took effect, inquiry calls flooded the city hall service office.

examples.ko: 민원실에서 서류를 발급받으면 관인이 선명하게 찍혔는지 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: When you get a document at the service office, check that the official seal is clearly stamped.
Until what time is the service office open?
The service office counters were very crowded.
A service office staff member kindly explained it to me.

examples.ko: 민원실로 가시면 바로 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go to the service office, you can apply right away.

explain: 시청, 구청, 주민센터에서 증명서를 떼거나 신청을 하는 곳이에요. 등본이나 증명서 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요. 대화에서는 그냥 '구청 가서 뗐어요'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the place in a city hall, ward office or community center where you get certificates or file requests. It often comes up when talking about resident registration copies or other certificates. In conversation people may just say '구청 가서 뗐어요' (I went to the ward office and got it).

examples.en: We notify the person who filed the request of the result by text message.
There were many people with requests, so I waited a long time.
The staff listen to the petitioner's story to the end.
Visitors with requests, please take a number and wait.

examples.ko: 화가 난 민원인을 차분하게 달래 줬어요.
examples.en: I calmly soothed the angry petitioner.
A person with a complaint came to the office.

explain: 관공서에 요청이나 불만을 넣는 사람을 말해요. 주로 공무원이나 기관 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요. 민원인 본인이 자기를 소개할 때는 보통 '문의드릴 게 있어서 왔어요'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It means a person who files a request or complaint with a government office. It is mostly used from the side of officials and institutions. People who are making a request usually don't call themselves this, and say something like '문의드릴 게 있어서 왔어요' (I came to ask about something).

examples.en: National character is hard to explain in a single word.

examples.ko: 그 책은 한국인의 민족성에 대해 다뤄요.
examples.en: That book deals with the national character of Koreans.
While traveling, I felt the different national character of each country.
You should use the word 'national character' carefully.
Talk about national character sometimes leads to misunderstandings.

examples.ko: 사람들은 민족성이 나라마다 다르다고 말하지만 사람마다 달라요.
examples.en: People say national character differs by country, but it differs by person.

explain: 한 민족이 가진 공통된 성격이나 특징이라는 생각을 담은 말이라서, 일반화처럼 들릴 수 있어요. 그래서 사람을 평가할 때는 조심해서 써요. 글이나 토론에서 더 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '국민성'이라는 말도 써요.
explain_en: It carries the idea of shared traits of an ethnic group, so it can sound like a generalization. Be careful when you use it to judge people. It shows up more in writing and discussion, and in everyday talk '국민성' is used too.

examples.ko: 이 리뷰는 과장이 너무 많아서 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: This review has too much exaggeration, so it's hard to believe.
I can't believe it ended this quickly.

examples.ko: 그 사람 말은 이상하게 잘 믿겨요.
examples.en: For some reason, what that person says is easy to believe.

examples.ko: 친구의 주장은 이유가 없어서 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: My friend's claim has no reasons behind it, so it's hard to believe.
Even after seeing it myself, I couldn't believe it.
At first, his excuse seemed believable.

explain: '믿다'의 피동형이라서 '내가 믿는' 게 아니라 '저절로 믿어지는' 느낌이에요. 가장 많이 쓰는 모양은 '믿기지 않다'로, 놀랍거나 기쁜 일에 '믿기지 않아요!'라고 말해요. '믿기 어렵다'는 의심스러운 내용에 써요.
explain_en: It is the passive of '믿다', so the feeling is not 'I believe' but 'it comes to be believed.' The most common form is '믿기지 않다', as in '믿기지 않아요!' for surprising or happy news. '믿기 어렵다' is used for content that seems doubtful.

examples.en: My shoe was swept away by the waves and disappeared.
I got pushed along by the crowd and ended up at the exit.

examples.ko: 지하철 문이 열리자 사람들 사이로 밀려갔어요.
examples.en: When the subway doors opened, I was pushed along among the people.
The boat is being pushed along by the wind.
The line is long, so I keep getting pushed back.
The sight of leaves drifting along on the ripples is pretty.

explain: '밀리다'(힘에 밀리다)에 '가다'가 붙어서, 내 뜻과 상관없이 어떤 방향으로 움직이는 모습이에요. 반대 방향은 '밀려오다'예요. 힘을 주어 미는 사람이 따로 있을 때는 '밀어 가다'가 아니라 '밀다'를 써요.
explain_en: It combines '밀리다' (be pushed) and '가다', showing something moving in a direction regardless of its own will. The opposite direction is '밀려오다'. When a person is deliberately pushing something, use '밀다' instead.

examples.en: At high tide the tidal flat is covered by water.
We have to go back before the tide comes in.
Today's high tide is around three in the afternoon.

examples.ko: 밀물과 썰물은 하루에 두 번씩 있어요.
examples.en: There are two high tides and two low tides a day.
The boat came into the harbor on the rising tide.
At rush hour people surged in like a tide.

explain: 반대말은 '썰물'이고, 둘이 같이 '밀물과 썰물'로 자주 나와요. 바닷물이 들어오는 때를 말해요. 사람이나 물건이 한꺼번에 몰려오는 모습을 '밀물처럼'이라고 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '썰물', and the two often appear together as '밀물과 썰물'. It means the time when seawater flows in. You can also say '밀물처럼' figuratively for people or things pouring in all at once.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 말투 때문에 밉상으로 보여요.
examples.en: That friend comes across as annoying because of the way they talk.
Even someone annoying grows on you the more you see them.

examples.ko: 회사에 밉상 동료가 한 명 있어요.
examples.en: There's one annoying coworker at my company.
You only pick the things that make people dislike you.

examples.ko: 저는 괜히 밉상이 된 것 같아요.
examples.en: I feel like I've become disliked for no reason.
My younger sibling is being really annoying today.

explain: 생김새보다는 하는 행동이나 말투 때문에 얄밉고 정이 안 가는 사람이라는 느낌으로 많이 써요. '밉상 짓', '밉상 동료'처럼 말해요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '귀염상'이나 '호감형'이에요.
explain_en: It is used more for someone who is annoying or hard to like because of their behavior or way of talking than because of their looks. You hear it in phrases like '밉상 짓' and '밉상 동료'. Words with the opposite feel are '귀염상' and '호감형'.

examples.en: I season the meat with salt and pepper beforehand.
Put the pre-seasoned chicken in the refrigerator.
I seasoned the fish before grilling it.
If you don't season it first, it tastes bland.
Season it first, then wait ten minutes.
My mother seasons the vegetables first before mixing them.

explain: 요리를 본격적으로 하기 전에 재료에 먼저 간을 해 두는 일이에요. 요리하면서 나중에 간을 맞추는 건 '간을 맞추다'라고 해요. 명사 '밑간'을 써서 '밑간을 하다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It means lightly seasoning the ingredients before the main cooking begins. Adjusting the taste later while cooking is '간을 맞추다'. You can also use the noun and say '밑간을 하다'.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 완성이 아니라 아직 밑그림이에요.
examples.en: This picture isn't finished; it's still just a rough sketch.
I drew the underdrawing first in pencil.
Try painting colors on top of the underdrawing.
You can feel the skill even from the underdrawing alone.

examples.ko: 이 계획은 아직 큰 밑그림일 뿐이에요.
examples.en: This plan is still just a big-picture outline.
The underdrawing was wrong, so I drew it again.

explain: 그림에서 색을 칠하기 전에 그리는 대략의 선 그림이에요. 계획이나 구상이 아직 대략적인 단계일 때 '밑그림을 그리다'라고 비유해서도 많이 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '스케치'도 쓰지만, 계획에는 밑그림이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is the rough line drawing made before applying color. It is also widely used figuratively, as in '밑그림을 그리다', when a plan is still at the rough stage. '스케치' is similar, but for plans '밑그림' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 실제 이야기를 밑바탕으로 썼어요.
examples.en: This novel was written with a true story as its basis.

examples.ko: 좋은 성적의 밑바탕에는 꾸준한 노력이 있어요.
examples.en: Steady effort lies at the foundation of good grades.
Trust is the foundation of every relationship.

examples.ko: 밑바탕을 먼저 칠하고 그 위에 그림을 그려요.
examples.en: I paint the base layer first and draw on top of it.

examples.ko: 기초 체력이 밑바탕이 되어야 오래 달려요.
examples.en: Basic stamina has to be the foundation for you to run for long.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 슬픔이 밑바탕에 깔려 있어요.
examples.en: Sadness runs underneath this song.

explain: 눈에 보이는 것 아래에 깔려 있는 바탕이라서, 생각이나 감정, 노력 같은 추상적인 것에 많이 써요. '기초'와 비슷하지만 '밑바탕'은 속에 깔려 있는 느낌이 더 강해요. '-을 밑바탕으로 하다'로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It means the base lying beneath what you can see, so it is often used for abstract things like ideas, feelings and effort. It is close to '기초', but '밑바탕' has a stronger sense of something lying underneath. A common pattern is '-을 밑바탕으로 하다' (to be based on).

examples.en: Selling at this price is a losing business.
You've got nothing to lose, so just ask once.
Boss, if you do this, we'll lose money.

examples.ko: 밑지고 파는 거라서 더 깎아 드릴 수 없어요.
examples.en: I'm selling at a loss, so I can't lower the price any more.
I worked all day and still lost money.

examples.ko: 한번 해 보세요. 밑질 게 없잖아요.
examples.en: Give it a try. You've got nothing to lose.

explain: 장사에서 판 값이 산 값보다 낮아서 손해를 보는 일을 말해요. 시장에서 가격을 깎을 때 상인이 '밑지고 파는 거예요'라고 자주 말해요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '남다'(이익이 남다)예요.

phrases.en: You have nothing to lose, so apply once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해 봐서 안 되어도 손해는 없으니 시도해 보라고 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to encourage someone to try, since failing costs nothing.

explain_en: In trade it means selling for less than you paid and taking a loss. At markets, vendors often say '밑지고 파는 거예요' when you ask for a discount. Its opposite in feel is '남다', as in '이익이 남다' (to make a profit).

examples.en: The department store started a bargain sale.
I bought a winter coat during the sale period.
Until when does this sale run?
It's a sale, so every shop is crowded.

examples.ko: 바겐세일 때는 반품이 안 되는 곳도 있어요.
examples.en: Some places don't accept returns during a sale.

examples.ko: 연말 바겐세일에 맞춰 신발을 사려고 해요.
examples.en: I plan to buy shoes during the year-end sale.

explain: 가격을 크게 낮추어 파는 세일을 말하며, 백화점이나 가게의 안내문에서 자주 봐요. 대화에서는 그냥 '세일'이라고만 해도 돼요. '세일하다'처럼 동사로 쓸 때는 '세일'을 써요.
explain_en: It means a sale with large price cuts, and you often see it on notices at department stores and shops. In conversation, just '세일' is fine. When you need a verb, use '세일' as in '세일하다'.

examples.en: The weekend market is teeming with people.
The pond is swarming with tadpoles.
It was vacation, so the amusement park was packed.

examples.ko: 식당 안이 손님으로 바글바글해서 못 들어갔어요.
examples.en: The restaurant was swarming with customers, so I couldn't get in.
I commute on a jam-packed subway.
Bugs swarming everywhere gives me goosebumps.

explain: 사람이나 작은 동물, 벌레가 한곳에 많이 모여 움직이는 모습을 흉내 낸 말이에요. '북적북적하다'와 비슷하지만 바글바글은 빽빽하게 가득한 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 '~이/가 바글바글해요'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It imitates the look of many people, small animals or bugs crowded and moving about in one place. It is similar to '북적북적하다', but '바글바글' has a stronger sense of being densely packed. It is usually used as '~이/가 바글바글해요'.

examples.en: Coming out into the outside world after a long time, the light was dazzling.
The child was curious about the outside world and just looked out the window.
I was only in the hospital, so I didn't know the news from outside.
Studying abroad showed me the wider world.
The outside world is bigger than you think.

examples.ko: 바깥세상과 연락이 끊긴 채 일주일을 지냈어요.
examples.en: I spent a week cut off from the outside world.

explain: 지금 내가 있는 집, 학교, 병원 같은 좁은 곳 밖의 넓은 세상을 말해요. 갇혀 있거나 오래 쉬다가 나왔을 때, 또는 경험이 좁았던 사람이 시야를 넓힐 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means the wide world beyond a small place such as your home, school or hospital. It is often used when someone comes out after being shut in or resting a long time, or when someone with limited experience widens their view.

examples.en: I caught a cold and couldn't go outside.
Grandmother finds it hard to go out these days.
I always wash my hands after going out.
Be careful about going outside when the fine dust is bad.
He stays at home without ever going out.
Bring a mask when you go out.

explain: 집 밖으로 나가고 들어오는 일을 말해요. '바깥출입을 삼가다', '바깥출입이 어렵다'처럼 건강, 날씨, 안전 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 평소 대화에서는 '외출'이나 '밖에 나가다'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It means going out of the house and coming back in. It often appears in talk of health, weather and safety, as in '바깥출입을 삼가다' (refrain from going out) and '바깥출입이 어렵다'. In ordinary conversation people more often say '외출' or '밖에 나가다'.

examples.en: Go stones come in black and white.
The child lined up the go stones in a row.
I'm upset because I lost one go stone.
We played five-in-a-row with go stones.
The go stones spilled onto the floor.
The sound of a go stone clicked sharply.

explain: 바둑을 둘 때 판 위에 놓는 검은 돌과 흰 돌을 말해요. '바둑알'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 돌을 놓을 때는 '바둑돌을 놓다/두다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the black and white stones placed on the board in go. '바둑알' is used with the same meaning. When placing a stone, you say '바둑돌을 놓다/두다'.

examples.en: The go board is full of stones.
My father brought out the go board.
The roads run neatly in a grid like a go board.

examples.ko: 바둑판은 가로세로 줄이 열아홉 개씩 있어요.
examples.en: A go board has nineteen lines in each direction.
I bought a checkered shirt.

examples.ko: 바둑판에서는 한 수 한 수가 중요해요.
examples.en: On the go board, every single move matters.

explain: 바둑을 두는 판이고, 가로세로로 줄이 반듯하게 그어져 있어서 격자무늬를 말할 때도 '바둑판무늬', '바둑판처럼'이라고 해요. 체스판은 '체스판'이라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It is the board on which go is played, and because it has neat lines running both ways, it is also used for grid patterns, as in '바둑판무늬' and '바둑판처럼'. A chessboard is called '체스판' separately.

examples.en: The child runs around holding a pinwheel.
When the wind blows, the pinwheel spins round and round.
A pinwheel doesn't spin without wind.
The child stopped in front of the pinwheel shop.
The garden decorated with pinwheels is pretty.
It's a dance that spins round and round like a pinwheel.

explain: 바람을 받아 빙글빙글 도는 장난감이에요. '바람개비를 돌리다'나 '바람개비가 돌다'처럼 말해요. 크게 만들어 놓은 풍력 발전기를 귀엽게 '바람개비'라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a toy that spins around when wind catches it. You say '바람개비를 돌리다' or '바람개비가 돌다'. People sometimes also affectionately call a big wind turbine a '바람개비'.

examples.en: My friend stood me up, so I watched the movie alone.
I got stood up on a blind date yesterday.
I called ahead in case I got stood up again.
I felt stood up and was gloomy all day.

examples.ko: 약속 시간이 지나도 안 와서 바람맞는 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: They didn't come even after the meeting time, so I thought I was being stood up.
I got stood up and waited a whole hour.

explain: 약속한 사람이 아무 말 없이 안 와서 혼자 남는 일을 말해요. 사람이 주어이고 '친구한테 바람맞다'처럼 '-한테'를 써요. 상대를 주어로 하면 '바람맞히다'가 돼요.
explain_en: It means being left on your own because the person you arranged to meet didn't show up and didn't tell you. The person left waiting is the subject, and the other person takes '-한테', as in '친구한테 바람맞다'. With the other person as subject, it becomes '바람맞히다'.

examples.en: He speaks straight in front of anyone.
Honest words are sometimes uncomfortable to hear.
It isn't easy to speak frankly to a superior.

examples.ko: 바른말 고운말을 쓰자는 포스터가 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: There's a poster urging people to use proper and kind language.

examples.ko: 친구가 해 준 바른말이 도움이 됐어요.
examples.en: The honest advice my friend gave me was helpful.
I only said what was right and ended up disliked.

explain: 뜻이 둘로 나뉘어요. 옳고 곧은 말(듣기 싫어도 맞는 말)을 뜻할 때는 '바른말을 하다'로 쓰고, 맞춤법이나 표준에 맞는 말을 뜻할 때는 '바른말 고운말'처럼 써요. 사실을 곧게 말하는 사람을 '바른말 잘하는 사람'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It has two senses. One is words that are right and straight, even if unpleasant to hear, as in '바른말을 하다'. The other is language that follows the correct standard, as in '바른말 고운말'. A person who speaks honestly is called '바른말 잘하는 사람'.
